qs.q: How can monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance be distinguished clinically from multiple myeloma?
o: MGUS uniformly causes hypercalcaemia and severe anaemia
MGUS features a bone marrow plasma cell count exceeding 30 percent
MGUS presents with elevated M protein without end-organ damage
MGUS presents with prominent renal failure and lytic bone lesions
qs.e: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance is defined by the presence of an elevated M protein without any associated end-organ damage such as CRAB features. Multiple myeloma is differentiated by the presence of both M protein and end-organ damage.
qs.s: Acute Leukaemia (AML/ALL) & WBC Disorders: Haematology Guide: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following conditions is associated with the presence of a monoclonal gammopathy alongside multiple myeloma?
qs.e: Waldenstrom’s microglobulinemia is one of the conditions explicitly associated with monoclonal gammopathy. Iron deficiency anemia is a benign hematologic condition not characterized by a malignant paraprotein spike.

qs.q: Which of the following features distinguishes monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) from multiple myeloma?
o: Elevated M protein without end-organ damage
qs.e: MGUS is defined by a monoclonal protein below myeloma-defining levels with no CRAB (calcium, renal, anaemia, bone) end-organ damage.
qs.s: Haematology Exam 2025: MCQs on Anaemia, Leukaemia & Clotting
